title: String Fundamentals: Creation, Formatting, and Indexing
objectives: Create strings with single, double, triple quotes
Format strings using f-strings with expressions
Access characters via indexing and slicing

content.title: String Creation and Quotes
content.explanation: Strings can be created with single, double, or triple quotes. Use different quotes to avoid escaping. Triple quotes allow multi-line strings.

content.title: String Creation Examples
content.code:
s4 = '''triple
single
quotes'''
s5 = 'It\'s working'
s6 =
print(s1, s2, s3, s4, s5, s6)
content.explanation: Choose quote style to minimize escaping. Triple quotes preserve newlines.

content.title: f-String Formatting
content.explanation: f-strings (formatted string literals) are the modern way to embed expressions in strings. Prefix with f or F, use {} for expressions.

content.title: f-String Examples
content.explanation: Expressions inside {} are evaluated and formatted. Format specifiers after : control output format.

content.title: Indexing and Slicing
content.explanation: Strings are sequences of characters. Access individual characters with square brackets. Use slices [start:stop:step] for substrings. Indices start at 0. Negative indices count from end.

content.title: Indexing and Slicing Examples
content.code:
print(text[0])      # P
print(text[-1])     # N
print(text[1:4])    # YTH
print(text[:3])     # PYT
print(text[3:])     # HON
print(text[::2])    # PTO
print(text[::-1])   # NOHTYP
content.explanation: Slice bounds are clamped - no IndexError for out-of-range slices.

content.title: Predict Slice Results
content.question: What are the outputs?
content.explanation: s[1:4]='BCD', s[-3:-1]='CD' (indices 3,4), s[::2]='ACE', out-of-range slice returns empty string.

content.title: Fix the String Error
content.error_message: IndexError: string index out of range
content.task: Fix the code to safely access the 10th character
content.hint: Check string length before indexing, or use slicing
